=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Issues Review (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Basis:** Seller counsel's update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003), with the baseline of 100% of Paperbark Analytics, AUD 24.0m, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law. I have not seen the underlying data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012), the Seller's full SPA draft, or the Buyer's own draft, so several recommendations depend on those. Market ranges are indicative and should be checked against current NSW deal practice.

**Known exposures in the Seller's own disclosure:** Riverlark ~AUD 3.2m, Sandbar AUD 330k, employee bonuses AUD 420k (plus on-costs), Ironquay AUD 180k open, and an unquantified privacy incident. Bluefen represents ~AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue. The disclosed specific items total ~AUD 4.13m, close to the Seller's proposed AUD 4.8m general cap. Once disclosed, these matters would largely fall outside warranty claims, so they need price adjustments or specific indemnities, not reliance on the warranty regime.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller position:** General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** A general cap at a materially higher level, ideally 30–100% of price, and in any case above the known specific exposures. Specific indemnities should sit outside this cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A 20% cap is at the low end for a buy-side position and leaves little room after disclosed items are excluded. *Reason: the disclosed matters alone could consume most of the cap.*

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller position:** AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible basket (only the excess is recoverable).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of ~AUD 10k or less, with related claims aggregated. Tipping basket (once exceeded, recovery from the first dollar), with basket ≈ 1% of price (~AUD 240k) at most. Fundamental and tax claims excluded from both.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible basket; push for a tipping basket. *Reason: a deductible basket removes the first AUD 250k of loss and the excess-only structure hits every claim.*

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller position:** 18 months from Completion. Seller proposes that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded.
- **Buyer wants:** 24–36 months for general warranties. Fundamental warranties at 6 years (the NSW contract limitation period). Tax claims at statute of limitations plus 60 days. Specific indemnities run to their own dates.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "applies to all Claims" wording and require carve-outs. *Reason: 18 months is short for financial and tax warranties, and the drafting would cut back fundamental and tax claims.*

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, solvency) capped at 100% of price, excluded from de minimis and basket, with a 6-year time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: title defects go to what the Buyer is paying for and should not be subject to general limits.*

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** Not addressed. Sections 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions do not apply to fraud, including fraud by the Seller or its agents.
- **Recommendation:** Add an express fraud carve-out and reject the "any nature" wording. *Reason: as drafted, the Seller's language arguably excludes fraud claims, and a fraud carve-out cannot be assumed to be implied.*

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 5pm 22 September 2026 (1.1) and of the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure only against specific warranties, with fair disclosure of the matter in reasonable detail. No general data room or public-register disclosure. Data room disclosure should be limited to the documents expressly listed, not everything referred to within them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosure. *Reason: general disclosure would let the Seller exclude the entire data room from warranty claims.*

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller position:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Deletion of the knowledge bar. Express pro-sandbagging wording so that Buyer knowledge does not prejudice claims. Exclusion only for matters specifically disclosed against a warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 8.3 and add an express pro-sandbagging clause. *Reason: the Buyer's diligence would otherwise defeat its own warranty claims, and under Australian law reliance on knowledge is not reliably resolved without express wording.*

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller position:** Consent "addressed"; Seller uses reasonable endeavours and treats consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter confirms no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Written Bluefen consent, in agreed form and with the 11.3 conditions satisfied, as a condition precedent or Completion deliverable. Buyer-only right to waive. If waived, a specific indemnity covering lost revenue or termination, backed by escrow or a price adjustment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject reasonable endeavours. Make consent a hard CP. *Reason: ~30% of revenue depends on it, and the Seller has not yet obtained it.*

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller position:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion. Not yet repaid.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price as Indebtedness, with a payout letter, discharge of all security (including PPSR registrations) and release of any share charges delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject a post-Completion release. Require payoff in the funds flow. *Reason: under debt-free/cash-free, the Seller must bear the debt, and a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer exposed to the lender.*

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller position:** AUD 420k conditional Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not in the funds flow. Payroll tax and on-costs are unaddressed.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses, plus employer payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs, treated as Seller costs and deducted from the price as debt-like items (or paid by the Seller through payroll before Completion). Specific indemnity for any employee claims arising from the bonus arrangements.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the exclusion from the funds flow. *Reason: the Buyer should not inherit a cost the Seller created and that arises from the transaction.*

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; considered "adequate." Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on payment of all SOW3 fees. AUD 180k is open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:** Full indemnity for all Ironquay claims and IP ownership defects, uncapped or at fundamental-level caps. Payment of the AUD 180k by the Seller before Completion (or deduction from price), and a confirmatory assignment as a CP.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: the Company may not own the IP it is relying on until SOW3 fees are paid.*

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. The Disclosure Letter says the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps), that it is unknown whether an unauthorised person accessed it, and that no loss amount has been stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Forensic investigation before signing or as a pre-Completion condition, with results shared. Specific indemnity for notification, regulatory, remediation and third-party costs, outside the general cap and time limits. Warranty on the absence of other incidents. Walk-away right or escrow if the investigation finds a notifiable breach.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "not material" as a characterisation. *Reason: the data involved is personal information, and the Company may have notification obligations under the Privacy Act's NDB scheme that the Buyer would inherit.*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller position:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k (AUD 110k each) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:** Full contract terms (term, termination rights, minimum commitments), reviewed alongside DD-008 and DD-011 for timing and scope. Any pre-Completion accrued amounts treated as debt-like or working capital. Interim covenant that renewals on new terms need Buyer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Accept only once terms are verified and any unavoidable post-Completion commitments are priced or excluded. *Reason: the Seller's characterisation is unsupported, and multi-year commitments can bind the Buyer after Completion.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** One regime for everything (caps, time limits, disclosure, knowledge and limitations).
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for (a) general warranties, (b) fundamental warranties, (c) tax indemnity, (d) specific indemnities (Bluefen, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy, Riverlark and any others), and (e) fraud. Each with its own cap, threshold and time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime. *Reason: a single regime lets general limits override the specific protections the Buyer needs for known risks.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller position:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. The Disclosure Letter confirms the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: ASIC company extract, inspection of the original share register and certificates, PPSR and other encumbrance searches (including any Riverlark security over the shares), and confirmation that the transfer chain is complete. Title warranty to be a fundamental warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Complete searches before signing and make title a fundamental warranty. *Reason: a register entry alone does not prove unencumbered title, and the Riverlark security makes encumbrance checks essential.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** A specific pre-Completion tax indemnity, uncapped to price, outside the de minimis and basket, with a limitation period of the statute of limitations plus 60 days. IP warranties covering ownership, non-infringement and the Ironquay materials, with ownership treated as fundamental.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: tax and IP exposures are typically unknown at signing and need dedicated protection rather than the general regime.*

---

### Priority actions
1. Require Bluefen written consent as a hard CP (SPA-N-008).
2. Require Riverlark payoff and discharge at Completion (SPA-N-009).
3. Price or indemnify bonuses, the Ironquay balance and the Sandbar commitments (SPA-N-010, 011, 013).
4. Commission a forensic review of the privacy incident before signing (SPA-N-012).
5. Restructure the regime into separate categories with fraud and fundamental carve-outs (SPA-N-004, 005, 014).
6. Complete independent title and encumbrance searches (SPA-N-015).

*Recommendations should be confirmed by NSW counsel against the full draft SPA and the underlying data room documents before they are sent to the Seller.*
